still_missing: The success criteria require absolute concentrations (e.g., μmol/g or μM) of inosine or specific SCFAs in paired tumor tissue and serum/stool from ICI-treated solid tumor patients. This study provides fecal SCFA concentrations and correlates them with outcomes and tumor gene expression, but it does not report the measured physiological concentrations of these metabolites inside the human tumor microenvironment. The specific intratumoral metabolite quantification remains unaddressed in the supplied text.
usable_content: This prospective study enrolled 39 patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (mNSCLC) treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) alone or with chemotherapy. The authors collected fecal and tumor samples prior to ICI initiation. Fecal short-chain fatty acids (SCFA) were measured by LC-MS/MS, and tumoral transcriptome profiling was performed via RNA sequencing. The study reported that high levels of fecal propionate correlated with significantly longer overall survival (p=0.02) and were increased in the high fiber diet group compared to the low fiber group. At the tumor level, RNA sequencing demonstrated upregulation of humoral and adaptive immune responses in the high fiber group. However, the text specifies fecal SCFA measurement and tumor transcriptomics; it does not explicitly report absolute concentrations of SCFAs or inosine within the tumor tissue itself.
